inputs.reported_history: step 0 continuation 0.8406; steps 11-419 continuation 0.8261, exact copy 0.4444; validation loss 0.914 -> 0.936

findings.claim: v0.0.25's published best.pt contains the unmodified v0.0.20 weights, so a v0.0.25-vs-v0.0.20 comparison has nothing to compare.
evidence: jobs/ember_hf_sft_v025.py seeds best_score with score(baseline, -1e9) and immediately writes best.pt at step=-1 from the freshly loaded v0.0.20 model.
score() orders (exact_copy, continuation_top1, clean_stop, teacher_forced, top5, top20, -mean_rank, -val_loss); the baseline's -val_loss term is +1e9, so a tie on every diagnostic loses.
Continuation fell to 0.8261 at step 11 and never recovered, and exact copy never rose, so no evaluated checkpoint ever beat the seeded baseline.
The reported final metrics are bit-identical to the step-0 baseline metrics, which is what re-loading that step=-1 checkpoint produces.
findings.consequence: The proposed case-by-case CPU diff between the v0.0.25 final model and v0.0.20 would report zero differences on all nine cases. It cannot produce a finding.

findings.claim: The v0.0.15 training curriculum cannot emit the character-level template of four of the five failing held-out values, so no amount of coverage repair drawn from it could fix them.
evidence: jobs/ember_curriculum_audit_v026.py reports FORMAT_GAP: 5 of 9 held-out templates have zero supporting rows in the 3600-row curriculum.
model_id: held out openai/gpt-6-astra has field signature [6a]/[3a]-[1d]-[5a]; every training model_id is vendor/ember-xxxx-NNb, i.e. [Na]/[5a]-[4ad]-[3ad]. First unsupported character is index 10.
url: held out https://example.test/a7Q9 is a single mixed-case segment; every training url has two segments.
path: held out /tmp/ember/Q7M4/result.json has no -xxxx leaf suffix; every training path does.
mixed: held out acct_Q7m4-5831 has an uppercase character in the account stem; every training stem is lower-cased.
The v0.0.25 trigger record confirms the dead end directly: 320 selected model_id coverage rows produced only 6 distinct target token ids and 7 distinct previous-token pairs.
findings.consequence: v0.0.21 through v0.0.25 added volume and loss shaping inside a template space that excludes the answer. The v0.0.24 'support_sparse' label was correct but under-read: the support is not sparse, it is absent, and it is absent by construction.

findings.claim: The learning rate has been annealed across versions until training became a no-op, which is why every metric froze for 400 steps.
evidence: At 1.8e-7 an AdamW step moves each weight by at most about the learning rate, so 420 steps bound total displacement near 7.6e-5 against typical weight magnitudes of 2e-2 to 5e-2.
Identical diagnostics at every evaluated step from 11 to 419 and a validation-loss drift of only 0.022 are the signature of that regime.
findings.consequence: v0.0.25 did not test its own hypothesis. Reading its flat result as 'filling coverage was not enough' is not supported; the run could not have shown a difference either way.

findings.claim: A nine-case battery cannot resolve the differences these runs are chasing, and it is also the checkpoint-selection objective rather than a held-out measurement.
evidence: exact_copy_rate is quantised to 1/9 = 11.1 points; the promotion gate at 0.5556 is one case above the current 0.4444.
The reported 0.8406 -> 0.8261 continuation change is 58/69 -> 57/69, a single token.
score() in jobs/ember_hf_sft_v016.py selects the saved checkpoint by exact_copy_rate on the same nine values that are reported as the held-out result.
findings.consequence: Ten runs were steered by a signal whose 95% interval on 4/9 spans roughly 0.19 to 0.73. Both the plateau and the apparent regressions are inside that interval.

findings.claim: The evaluation prompt itself is off-distribution in both distractor slots.
evidence: prompt_for() in jobs/ember_hf_sft_v015.py hard-codes 'Ignore old=K2P8 and fallback=77291'.
K is reserved for the validation prefix alphabet, so no training target begins with it, and every training digits value has eight digits rather than five.
Training prompts draw both distractors from the same generator as the target.
findings.consequence: All nine evaluation prompts carry a slot pattern the model never saw during v0.0.15 through v0.0.25.

findings.claim: Exactly one failing case, digits, is a genuine representation problem rather than a curriculum gap.
evidence: The audit reports the digits template as fully supported with 400 rows.
v0.0.24 independently labelled it deep_context_miss_with_support, with expected_rank 59 and support_same_kind_offset 7, against support_sparse for the other four.
The model predicted piece '84' where '4' was expected: a segmentation choice, not a missing structure.
findings.consequence: Tokenizer or representation work is warranted for digits, and only for digits. It is worth at most 1 of the 9 legacy cases, so it is not the reason the other four fail.

recommended_next_phase.strategy: format-parity curriculum, restored learning rate, 90-case battery
notes: Do not run the v0.0.25-vs-v0.0.20 case diff; finding F1 shows the two checkpoints are the same weights.
Do not change the tokenizer or the model size yet; findings F2 and F3 are cheaper and are not ruled out.
Give every held-out template supporting rows in training, verified by jobs/ember_curriculum_audit_v026.py --assert-parity in CPU CI.
Restore the learning rate to a value that can move the model; 1.2e-6 sits between the last effective run (v0.0.16 at 2.5e-6) and the frozen regime.
Grow the battery to 90 cases so a real change is distinguishable from a single string, and keep the legacy nine verbatim as the v0.0.20 protection metric.
Draw the evaluation prompt's distractors from the training distribution, and keep the legacy prompt for the protected comparison.
Drop the neighbour and hard-kind mining fractions for one run. They were added to compensate for the missing structure; with parity restored, a simpler run is interpretable.
Treat digits as a separate representation experiment after v0.0.26 reports.
